subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a public normal-chat tool-error delivery policy such as `all | final | off`, or keep the current boolean `messages.suppressToolErrors` plus default-visible mutating warnings?
rationale: The remaining change is not a narrow bug fix: it adds public config surface and changes when users see failed side effects after an apparently successful turn.

options.title: Add a conservative opt-in policy
options.body: Keep current default behavior, then add a documented opt-in mode for hosted/team deployments with focused tests for safe failure visibility and suppression.

options.title: Keep the existing boolean only
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors: true` as the operator escape hatch and decline success-aware suppression until a clearer safety model exists.

options.title: Defer to run-loop recovery design
options.body: Route this need into broader native tool-failure recovery work so the agent can explicitly resolve or narrate failures instead of relying on delivery filtering.

recommendation.title: Add a conservative opt-in policy
recommendation.body: Keep current default behavior, then add a documented opt-in mode for hosted/team deployments with focused tests for safe failure visibility and suppression.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc most recently carried the warning-policy behavior and the merged PR that explicitly left this broader policy question open.
